senses: A striking and vivid representation or scene; a picture.
A vivid graphic scene of a group of people or objects arranged as in a painting or bas relief sculpture.
An arrangement of actors in static positions on stage, having the effect of pointing up a particular moment in the drama, conventionally revealed by opening tableau curtains (known as "tabs").
Mostly in solitaire card games, but also in other card and board games, the main area, where random cards can be arranged.
A unit of a play, an opera, or a ballet with change of stage setting.
ety: Unadapted borrowing from French tableau, from Old French tablel (“a surface which is used primarily for painting”).

senses: A liquor distilled from grapes (a brandy) made in wine-producing regions of Peru and Chile. It is the most widely consumed spirit in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish pisco, from the name of the city Pisco, from Quechua pishku, pisqu.

senses: To mix too thoroughly
examples: Don’t overmix; it’s O.K. if a few lumps remain.

senses: A premaxilla.
Exhibiting braggadocio; characterized by empty boasts.
A man who spends time in outdoor pursuits or sports.
The office or position of a curate.
A person who spends money.
A victim of rape.
Spanish dry-cured ham
ety: From Spanish jamón. Doublet of gammon and jambon.

senses: A policeman assigned to an intersection to direct the traffic.
Synonym of endman (“type of stock minstrel character”).
A person who undergoes psychoanalysis; one who is analysed.
An administrator or moderator who behaves badly.
A structure design in which the frame and body are built as a single integrated structure.
ety: First attested in 1914: from the French monocoque.

senses: The portion of an address comprising the street number and the street name, such as 3912 Park Drive.
ety: Borrowed from Latin situs (“position, site”). Doublet of site and sitio.

senses: Synonym of hawala (“informal system of money transfer from India and the Middle East”).
A collection box used in Indian temples to collect cash offerings from devotees.
ety: Borrowed from Gujarati and Kachchi હૂંડી (huṇḍī), and Hindustani (Hindi हुंडी (huṇḍī) / Urdu ہُنْڈی (huṇḍī)), ultimately derived from Sanskrit हुण्डिका (huṇḍikā).

senses: A supporter of productivism.
One who lays up or forms a store.
examples: Offer the PCB waste to transporters, disposers, or commercial storers of PCB waste who have not received an EPA identification number.

senses: To let a property again
One who adheres to the theory or method of impressionism.
A performer who does impressions; a mimic.
One who bears the gonfalon.
An official, particularly a chief magistrate of a mediaeval Italian republic; the bearer of the republic's gonfalon.
ety: From Middle English gonfalonier, from Old French gonfalonier.

senses: The property of being optimal.
Having a knee or knees, or, in combination, the stated type of knee or knees.
Refusing to proceed or cooperate.
Ankylosaurus magniventris, a large herbivorous dinosaur of the Cretaceous period notable for its heavy armor and clublike tail.
ety: From taxonomic name Ankylosaurus, from ankylo- + -saurus, from Ancient Greek ἀγκύλος (ankúlos, “crooked”) + New Latin -saurus, from Ancient Greek σαῦρος (saûros, “lizard”). The word was coined in 1908 without explanation by Barnum Brown and may refer to his mistaken belief that its back was sharply bent in a manner similar to the stegosaurus or to his attention to the fusion of his specimens' rear ribs to their vertebrae, a condition medically known as ankylosis.

senses: The ability of a solid surface to reduce the surface tension of a liquid in contact with it such that it spreads over the surface and wets it.
A pit in which hides are stored.
The system of accepting a deposit and holding for a customer to complete a purchase.
An item which has been held in this way.
ety: Deverbal from lay away. The truly solidified verb (as contrasted with the merely misspelled one) is back-formed from the noun but is nonstandard.
examples: A chain of local gun shops advertised, as a “Father's Day Sale,” the semiautomatic Intratec TEC-9, with extra ammo clip, case, and flash suppressor, reduced from $347.80 to $249.95 and available on layaway.

senses: A women's suit consisting of coordinated pants (trousers) and jacket
A person who tweaks something.
A tool, especially a screwdriver, for making small adjustments.
ety: From tweak + -er; the drug addict sense derives from the slang term tweak for methamphetamines, in reference to the punding behavior of addicts.
examples: That attack may damage the homosexual, but even as he is hurt, he also feels superior, because he is not a bull—a blind, stupid animal. Rather, he is an aesthete—a tweaker, not a charger.

senses: A fur containing a pattern of pigmentation in which individual hairs have several bands of light and dark pigment with black tips; any of several genes responsible for this pigmentation.
ety: From French agouti, from Old Tupi akuti. The name of the acouchi is probably from the same source.

senses: A tribe or group of people in Ireland, having a loose voluntary system of governance entered into through contracts by all members.
The opening produced in such incision.
The act or process of making brutal
An instance of being brutalized.
A young girl.
A woman or person with feminine traits.
examples: Near-synonyms: baby girl; see also Thesaurus:girl

senses: Childish; immature.
Of, like, or suitable for a child.
examples: So! here I find on kiddish mind / Traditionary lore instil'd. / Tho' fairly bookt, Nymph might have lookt / For poet's promise unfulfil'd.
It had caught my eye specifically because of the shiny packaging and how like kiddish it sort of looked, so I thought it might to be fun to try on.

senses: A Mediterranean dish of cured fish roe
ety: Borrowed from Italian bottarga. Doublet of tarek.
examples: In case you’re wondering, my foodstuff was about six pounds of bottarga.

senses: A substance (such as calcium oxide or silica gel) that is used as a drying agent because of its high affinity for water.
ety: Derived from Latin dēsiccans, active present participle of dēsiccō, from dē- (“of; from, away from”) + siccō (“dry up”).

senses: A simple eye consisting of a single lens and a small number of sensory cells.
An eyelike marking in the form of a spot or ring of colour, as on the wing of a butterfly or the tail of a peacock.
ety: From Latin ocellus (“little eye”), from oculus (“eye”).

senses: One who, or that which, dulls.
examples: But, of all, your grace must fly phlebotomy, fresh pork, conger, and clarified whey: they are all dullers of the vital spirits.

senses: Having a ghastly appearance; weird.
ety: Poetic abbreviation of ghastly. Use as a noun influenced by ghost.
